scope.significance: Opens Clause 10 with the expression grammar built in precedence layers.

authoring.author_context: fresh subagent context in an isolated worktree based on 069d85e

precedence_structure.independently_derived_by_reviewer: primary -> defined unary -> ** -> * / -> unary + - -> binary + - -> // -> one relation -> .NOT. -> .AND. -> .OR. -> .EQV./.NEQV. -> defined binary
precedence_structure.author_initial_summary: primary -> defined unary -> power/mult/add -> concat -> rel -> logical -> defined binary
precedence_structure.verdict: The author's initial summary matched only coarsely; the catalogue text was corrected to the finer chain, separating ** from * /, unary from binary + -, and the four logical levels.
precedence_structure.why_it_matters: A layer confusion here would silently corrupt every later expression requirement.

findings.defect: A literal-value oracle was proposed for the left grouping of concatenation, but character concatenation is associative, so both parenthesisations produce the same string and the oracle cannot observe the grouping.
findings.correction: The plan admits only the final value and records that the grouping is not observable by value for intrinsic operands.

findings.defect: An execution-path oracle was proposed for .AND. grouping. Fortran does not require short-circuit evaluation, so a processor may evaluate operands in any order or not at all; grouping cannot be inferred from which operand was evaluated.
findings.correction: The execution-path oracle was removed and the limitation recorded.

findings.defect: The .EQV./.NEQV. grouping plan was neither concrete nor checkable, and those operations are associative in two-valued logic.
findings.correction: Replaced with an explicit statement of the limitation for intrinsic operands.

findings.defect: A right-operand defined-binary negative attributed an applicability or generic-resolution failure to R1023 syntax. A program whose defined operator has no applicable specific procedure is not rejected by the R1023 form.
findings.correction: The facet is now a positive boundary only, with applicability and generic resolution assigned to their real owners 10.1.6 and 15.4.3.4.2 as dependencies. The reviewer confirmed the form itself remains positively tested.

findings.defect: The replacement text for C10ER-001 to C10ER-003 claimed unobservability too broadly. Those operations are associative only for intrinsic operands; a non-associative defined extension of the same operator symbol makes the grouping observable by value.
findings.correction: Each affected plan now scopes the unobservability claim to intrinsic operands and records the non-associative defined-extension route as the concrete future shape, with 10.1.6 and 15.4.3.4.2 cited as the owners of the defined-operation semantics.
findings.note: Raised against the corrected text rather than the original packet, and a reminder that a convenient unobservability claim is itself a defect if it is too broad.

explicit_limitations: Source registration only: no test program, compiler invocation, oracle, canonical link, SourceUse relationship or fixture approval is created.
All 187 facets remain pending. Several grouping facets are explicitly unobservable for intrinsic operands and record a defined-extension route rather than an implemented program.

Expression interpretation, evaluation and constant expressions remain owned by 10.1.3 through 10.1.12; intrinsic assignment by the registered 10.2.1.3; designators by the Clause 9 catalogues; defined operations by 15.4.3.4.x.
Clause 10 is only opened by this packet: 10.1.3 onwards and most of 10.2 remain unauthored.
